quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does it mean when you make eye contact with another driver?

options.text: They see you.
It does not mean they will yield to you properly.
They will definitely yield to you properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that a driver will yield to you just because they looked at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still do not see them.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, push slightly on the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what tire adjustment will you likely need?

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Do not change the tire pressure.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You will need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, where should you position yourself?

options.text: So the driver can see you in their side mirror.
So the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
So the driver can see you through the passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of your lane behind the car. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?

options.text: In the front.
Just behind the lead rider.
In the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets more experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: The center of a lane has an oily strip. What should you know about this strip?

options.text: Always avoid it.
It is safe to ride on unless it is raining.
Only ride on it if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to ride on unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except when it is raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center lane.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind it.
Stop and wait for it to start moving.
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space and proceed with caution. Slow down and be ready to stop when approaching an emergency scene.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, each motorcyclist should pass one at a time. One rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: Shifting gears while in a curve:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause the motorcycle to skid.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you:

options.text: May exceed the speed limit by 10 mph.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Are required to ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must stay within the speed limit while passing. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Motorcycles face the greatest risk of conflict with other traffic:

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Slow down and be careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You have space to maneuver.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Lanes with traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is slippery.
The sun is shining.
You believe stopping will be routine.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy and another driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while you are stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked. You can usually control the motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, you should:

options.text: Get off the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left track often works best, but this can change based on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, eye protection is:

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders must use proper eye protection when riding in Georgia.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show more of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. They also make objects look farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to convex mirrors on your motorcycle.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Give you an escape route.
Help you feel wind blasts.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you feel wind blasts.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to see better.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull to the side of the road and wait for it to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads become slippery when rain first starts, especially in the center of the lane. When rain begins, ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: Helmets are:

options.text: Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers.
Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 18.
Required for passengers, but not riders.
Not required for anyone on a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 18.
questions.explanation: In Idaho, all motorcycle riders and passengers under age 18 must wear helmets. All riders and passengers of any age should wear helmets for safety.

questions.question: If carrying a load, the load should be:

options.text: Secured as low as possible.
Secured as high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: If not using saddlebags, secure loads as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can affect balance.
